html:
The map's label, in its 700 snapshot, for the peoples of the south-western Ethiopian highlands, beyond the reach of Aksum. They spoke Cushitic, Omotic and some Semitic languages and farmed enset, grains and cattle on the cool, rainy plateau, much as the earlier highland farmers had.

Written records say little about them in this period. Later centuries saw kingdoms rise here, such as Damot and Kaffa, the land often linked with the origin of coffee, before the Ethiopian Empire conquered the region in the late 1800s.
